sections.heading: Presidential Medal Rules and Limits
sections.body: Executive Order 11085 permits the medal for especially meritorious contributions to U.S. security or national interests, world peace, or significant public or private endeavors. The order allows a president to choose recipients from recommendations or on the president’s own initiative, without requiring congressional approval or a judicial proceeding. It establishes an honorary recognition and does not provide a process for changing attorney discipline.

sections.heading: Giuliani’s Election Conduct and Disbarment
sections.body: New York’s Appellate Division found in 2024 that Giuliani repeatedly and intentionally made false statements about the 2020 election and ordered his immediate disbarment. The court directed him to stop practicing law, appearing as an attorney, giving legal advice or holding himself out as a lawyer unless a later court order permits it. The District of Columbia Court of Appeals imposed reciprocal disbarment on Sept. 26, 2024, effective nunc pro tunc to Aug. 9, 2021.

event_overview.subject: Gaza Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Gaza Conflict refers here to the war and continuing violence involving Israel, Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups that followed the 7 October 2023 attacks from Gaza into Israel and Israel’s subsequent military campaign in the Gaza Strip. A ceasefire took effect on 10 October 2025 and ended large-scale hostilities, but United Nations reporting as of 21 November 2026 described continued Israeli strikes, shooting and shelling, Palestinian casualties, access restrictions and severe humanitarian needs in Gaza.

facts.label: Start and current status
facts.value: The present war began on 7 October 2023, when Palestinian armed groups from Gaza attacked communities and military sites in southern Israel and Israel began strikes on Gaza. A ceasefire effective 10 October 2025 ended large-scale hostilities but did not end violence.

facts.label: Location and principal parties
facts.value: The core theatre is the Gaza Strip and nearby areas of Israel. The conflict involves Israeli forces and Hamas alongside other Palestinian armed groups; civilians in Gaza and Israel have been directly affected.

facts.label: Pre-war context
facts.value: The United Nations describes Gaza as having been under an Israeli blockade of varying intensity since 2007, with recurrent escalations between Israeli forces and Palestinian armed groups before the 2023 war.

facts.label: Humanitarian and diplomatic framework
facts.value: UN Security Council Resolution 2728, adopted on 25 March 2024, demanded a Ramadan ceasefire leading to a lasting sustainable ceasefire, release of hostages, humanitarian access and compliance with international law. The 2025 ceasefire was supported by mediation involving Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye and the United States.

facts.label: International legal proceedings
facts.value: South Africa instituted proceedings against Israel at the International Court of Justice on 29 December 2023 under the Genocide Convention. The Court has issued provisional-measures orders; these are interim directions and do not decide the case’s final merits.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War is the 2026 regional armed conflict involving the United States, Iran and Israel, with effects extending to Gulf states, the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea and Yemen. It has combined military operations, attacks and restrictions affecting commercial shipping, diplomatic efforts to halt fighting, and U.S. domestic disputes over presidential war powers.

facts.label: Conflict timeline
facts.value: A United Nations economic assessment dates the start of the conflict to February 28, 2026. A ceasefire took effect on April 8, but the UN reported renewed hostilities from early July after a de-escalation framework was not fully implemented.

facts.label: Geographic and economic significance
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz is a central focus because conflict-related restrictions and attacks disrupted commercial passage and energy exports from the Gulf; the UN said average daily ship transits fell sharply from 2025 levels during 2026.

facts.label: Diplomatic framework
facts.value: The United States and Iran signed the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding on June 17, 2026. Pakistan and Qatar participated as mediators in follow-up talks, intended to advance implementation and de-escalation.

facts.label: U.S. war-powers issue
facts.value: Congressional debate centers on the War Powers Resolution, which provides for termination of certain uses of U.S. armed forces absent a declaration of war or specific statutory authorization and describes congressional direction by concurrent resolution in section 5(c).

facts.label: July 23 House action
facts.value: On July 23, 2026, the House adopted H.Con.Res. 89 by 214-208. Its title directed the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a short late-July 2026 period of escalation, congressional action, maritime and regional spillover, and ceasefire talks; it does not provide a complete account of the conflict’s origins, all military operations, humanitarian consequences, or subsequent developments.

event_overview.title: About Space Exploration
event_overview.subject: Space Exploration
event_overview.summary: The event centers on SpaceX’s Starship Flight 15 test, which demonstrated recovery of the Starship upper stage at Starbase, Texas after an orbital mission. The result is significant because SpaceX is developing Starship as a two-stage system intended for rapid reuse, while NASA’s Voyager 1 milestone illustrates a separate, long-running strand of space exploration: robotic science beyond the heliosphere.

facts.label: Mission timing and location
facts.value: Flight 15 launched from SpaceX’s Starbase site near Boca Chica in Cameron County, Texas, on November 13, 2026; the Starship upper stage returned to the site and was caught by the launch tower on November 14. The selected timeline’s November 15 date reflects subsequent reporting rather than the capture’s calendar date.

facts.label: Vehicle format
facts.value: Starship is a two-stage launch system comprising the Starship upper stage and the Super Heavy booster. SpaceX’s stated design approach is for both stages to return to Earth and be caught by mechanical arms on the launch tower for inspection, refurbishment, and reuse.

facts.label: Test outcome
facts.value: The upper stage completed an orbital flight and was recovered at the launch tower, while the Super Heavy booster diverted to a water landing rather than completing its planned tower catch.

facts.label: Regulatory setting
facts.value: Commercial Starship/Super Heavy launches from Boca Chica are regulated by the Federal Aviation Administration’s Office of Commercial Space Transportation. FAA licensing reviews address public safety, national-security and foreign-policy concerns, insurance, and environmental effects.

facts.label: Related Voyager milestone
facts.value: On November 18, 2026, NASA’s Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth—about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 launched in 1977 and is managed by NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

event_overview.scope_note: This selected Muninn timeline covers the Starship recovery milestone and Voyager 1’s one-light-day distance milestone, not a complete history of Starship testing, NASA exploration missions, or all spaceflight developments.

event_overview.title: About West Bank Violence
event_overview.subject: West Bank Violence
event_overview.summary: West Bank violence refers to recurring attacks, confrontations and other coercive incidents affecting Palestinians, Israeli settlers and Israeli forces across the West Bank, including damage to people, homes, farmland, livestock and essential infrastructure. The November 2026 developments concern alleged settler attacks on Palestinian communities within a wider pattern that UN humanitarian monitors document separately from other forms of violence in the territory.

facts.label: Location and context
facts.value: The West Bank, including East Jerusalem, is treated by the United Nations and the International Court of Justice as part of the Occupied Palestinian Territory; the ICJ’s July 19, 2024 advisory opinion addressed Israeli policies and practices there, including settlements and settler violence.

facts.label: Legal framework
facts.value: UN Security Council Resolution 2334, adopted in 2016, states that Israeli settlements in Palestinian territory occupied since 1967, including East Jerusalem, have no legal validity under international law. Israel disputes this characterization and maintains claims and security positions concerning the territory.

facts.label: How incidents are tracked
facts.value: OCHA has documented West Bank casualties since 2005 and settler violence since 2006, counting settler attacks that result in Palestinian casualties, property damage, or both.

facts.label: Recent pattern
facts.value: OCHA recorded more than 1,600 settler attacks causing Palestinian casualties and/or property damage from January through mid-September 2026, affecting 275 Palestinian communities; reported effects included injuries, arson and damage to homes, crops, water systems and other infrastructure.

facts.label: Displacement impact
facts.value: OCHA reported that settler attacks and related access restrictions displaced more than 6,500 Palestinians between January 2023 and August 2026, alongside damage to livelihoods and essential services.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline follows the selected November 22, 2026 attacks and related Israeli political reaction; it does not attempt to catalogue all West Bank violence, settlement activity, military operations, legal claims or wider Israeli-Palestinian conflict developments.
